coachingPoints: The zone moves on every pass — ball-you-man positioning on every catch
The top two must take away the middle; nothing splits the zone cleanly
Close out to shooters with high hands — zones die on uncontested threes
Rebounding is everyone's job — find a body, because nobody has 'your man'
Talk through every rotation — zones without communication are just standing
commonMistakes: Standing in spots instead of shifting with the ball — a static zone is a shooting drill
Letting the ball get to the middle of the zone — the high post kills 2-3
Forgetting to rebound — the offense gets three chances per possession
The wings failing to bump the high-post flash — free catches in the middle
description: The 2-3 zone: two guards up top, three across the back — alignment, rotations, and how to stop the high post.

diagram.title: 2-3 zone shifts toward the ball side

gameSituations: Against teams that struggle to shoot from outside
To protect bigs in foul trouble — less one-on-one exposure
After timeouts as a change-up look that disrupts rhythm
When your team is tired — the zone covers ground with less running

howTo.detail: Set two defenders at the top — near the elbows extended — and three across the back: two wings at the blocks extended and one middle defender protecting the rim.
howTo.title: Align in the 2-3 shape

howTo.detail: Every defender positions between the ball, themselves, and the basket. When the ball is on the left, the whole zone slides left; the shape moves as one connected unit.
howTo.title: Shift with the ball

howTo.detail: The top two defenders take the ball and the wings. Nobody lets a dribbler split the middle of the zone — the guards funnel everything to the sides.
howTo.title: Protect the middle

howTo.detail: When the ball goes to a wing, the nearest back-line defender closes out with high hands while the middle defender slides toward the ball side. The weak-side wing sinks to the middle.
howTo.title: Rotate on wing catches

howTo.detail: The high post is the zone's weak spot. The middle defender must bump or front any flash to the high post, and the wings must help deny the entry.
howTo.title: Take away the high post

howTo.detail: On every shot, each defender finds the nearest offensive player and boxes out. Zone rebounding is assignment-by-proximity, drilled until it is habit.
howTo.title: Rebound by proximity

title: 2-3 Zone Defense
whatIsIt: The 2-3 zone is the most common zone defense in basketball: two defenders across the top and three across the bottom, each responsible for an area rather than a player. The shape looks like a wall — hard to penetrate, easy to understand, and excellent at protecting the paint.

Zones work by keeping five defenders between the ball and the basket at all times. The 2-3 is especially strong against teams that cannot shoot, because it packs the lane and forces the offense to win from outside. Its weakness is equally clear: good shooting teams can pick it apart, and rebounding requires extra discipline since nobody has a set box-out assignment.
whyItMatters: The 2-3 zone is every player's first introduction to team defensive concepts — shifting with the ball, protecting the middle, closing out from help. It lets less athletic teams compete, protects players in foul trouble, and gives coaches a reliable change-up. Learning to play it — and learning to attack it — is fundamental basketball education.
